A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 29 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations and figures.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–3 report original experiments on synthetic data, IMDB and Yelp, including trained-embedding measurements and convergence-loss comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains these original synthetic-data and sentiment-classification experiments, with experimental settings documented in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The attention architectures, logistic objective, and analyzed procedure of one embedding-update step followed by gradient flow on p are unchanged. The revisions concern their theoretical analysis.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic token-generation model and IMDB/Yelp binary sentiment tasks. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same one-layer and two-layer attention models are examined. No empirical comparison method is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the preprocessing, plotted quantities and training settings, including embedding dimension 2048, batch size 128, and 500 real-data versus 196 synthetic-data training epochs. Revised theoretical dimension bounds do not change the experimental settings.

E4.justification: The token-importance analyses and checks across synthetic data, real data and model depth are retained unchanged. No additional ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis or error analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both versions retain token-level scatter plots and mean curves without reporting repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 contain identical plotted results. Section 5 also retains convergence-loss orders of 10^-5 for the two-layer model and 10^-1 for the one-layer model on IMDB and Yelp.

T1.justification: Lemma 4.2 drops the pseudoinverse characterization and claim that all margin constraints are tight. Lemma 4.5 revises its dimension requirements. Appendix C.3 adds a projected full-row-rank construction, while Appendix C.4 adds Lemmas C.7–C.8 and substantially rebuilds the proof using tight-constraint subsets, a solution-norm bound and additional error estimates.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: one-step learning of token frequencies, max-margin token selection under directional convergence, and sufficient conditions for excluding irrelevant tokens.

C2.justification: The qualitative interpretations of embedding correlations and token selection are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitation to first-order token statistics and the same conjecture about causal structure and deeper attention models.

D1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same preprocessing instructions, tokenizer, optimizer, hyperparameters and data-access references. No implementation or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, comparison with TLZO23 in Section 4.2 and bibliography are unchanged. No cited work or substantive research-positioning claim is added or removed.

P1.justification: Localized prose edits accompany the shortened Lemma 4.2, clarified rank argument and reorganization of Appendix C.4 around auxiliary lemmas. The overall section hierarchy and main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Theorem 4.3 and its proof sketch now fit together on one page, and surrounding text, footnotes and references reflow. Figures 1–3 retain identical panels, axes, legends and captions; no figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: v1's Appendix C.2 incorrectly treats inequality-constrained KKT conditions as forcing every constraint to equality, and its Lemma 4.5 proof relies on that claim. v3 removes this overclaim and substantially reconstructs the dependent argument using tight-constraint analysis and explicit bounds, while also repairing the projected-rank construction. These changes materially improve the theoretical foundation of a central contribution, at the cost of stricter dimension requirements; the empirical evidence remains unchanged.
